title: Finding the double check in a mixed set
outcomes: Finds the double check that mates or wins material when no theme is named
Lists the king's flight squares to decide whether the double check finishes
Says that a move is not a double check when a piece blocks the uncovered line

steps.text: From **Double check** you know a double check is two checks from one move. Now you must find one in a mixed set, and say so when there is none. Scan for a piece that stands in front of a line to the king and could also give check by moving. Then count the king's squares: it can only move, so look for covered flight squares.

steps.caption: White to move. One rook move gives two checks.

line.say: The rook checks along the eighth rank and uncovers the queen's check from c4 along the diagonal.

steps.text: Against a double check, capturing and blocking are impossible: only a king move is legal. Three questions before you play. Does the moving piece itself give check? Is the uncovered line really open? Are all the king's flight squares covered? **Rule of thumb:** if a double check does not mate, count what the forced king move gives up, since the king may simply step to a better square.

steps.title: Is it still a double check?
steps.prompt: One pawn stands on e7. Predict whether Nf6+ is checkmate.
Which did you check first: the second line, or the king's flight squares? What would you check first next time?
